title: Authority grant (capability token)
description: What an agent invocation is BOUNDED by. Every bound is a required field, because a bound that is not written down is not a bound -- an omitted scope reads as unlimited to anyone reading the grant. Authority is explicit, scoped, expiring and NON-TRANSITIVE: there is no delegation field, and `may_delegate` is prohibited by name so that adding one is a schema change a reviewer sees rather than a property that quietly appears. The framework's load-bearing separation: runtime identity != role != capability != authority. All four resolve independently. Identity lives in config/agent_identity_registry.schema.json (FWK-081) and is NOT redefined here. Canonical serialization: UTF-8 JSON, keys sorted, separators (',',':'). Digest is sha256 over those bytes as 'sha256:<hex>'. Backward compatibility: additive optional fields are minor; removing a field, narrowing an enum or adding a required field is MAJOR and takes a new $id.

work_package_id.description: No work package, no work. A grant with no subject authorises open-ended action.

issued_by.description: Never equal to agent_id: an agent may not issue its own authority.

expires_at.description: Authority expires. A grant with no expiry is a standing permission that outlives the work it was issued for.

permitted_paths.description: An empty path list is not 'anywhere', it is an unclassified grant.

tool_allowlist.description: What the authority engine GRANTED -- distinct from the agent's tool_requests, which is what it asked for. Tool availability is capability, not permission.

required_evidence.description: Declared at grant time, not chosen at closure time. Evidence selected after the fact is evidence selected to fit.

confers_merge_authority.description: const false at A3. Merge authority is retained by the operator; a grant able to express it would let it be granted by writing a field.

may_delegate.description: Authority is non-transitive. Named and pinned false so that transitivity cannot arrive as an undeclared default.

identity_ref.description: Optional pointer into the agent identity registry. Identity is resolved there, not restated here; a grant that carried its own identity claim would let a holder assert both what it is and what it may do.
